findings.text: Shared superblock acquisition is offered as a nonblocking predicate. It reports success only when the shared hold was obtained and the instance is neither marked dying nor missing a root nor missing born status; any other outcome releases the hold and reports failure.

Four globally visible writeback activation paths exist: a workqueue handler that drains a backing writeback object, a dontcache kick that marks dontcache work once per dirty device and wakes it with a held reference, a global wakeup that iterates all backing devices under read side protection, and a per superblock best effort kick that proceeds only when the shared superblock hold is immediately available.

Filesystem parameter parsing exposes lookup plus layered handlers. Lexical lookup resolves a name in a null terminated table with a caller supplied fallback. Source handling accepts only one key with string type and rejects repeated assignment. The main dispatcher validates presence of a key then tries superblock flags, security policy, filesystem specific parsing, and finally source fallback before failing as unknown. Companion helpers adapt counted strings and split monolithic blobs with a caller supplied separator, with a comma variant provided.

Filesystem context lifecycle exposes creation for reconfigure and submount plus duplication and logging. Reconfigure refuses kernel internal instances. Submount creation applies a security check with cleanup on denial. Duplication requires a filesystem supplied duplicator, shallow copies the descriptor, reinitializes its mutex, clears private pointers, takes references on type and namespaces and credentials and log, then invokes filesystem and security duplicators with cleanup on failure.

Per superblock writeback scans the IO queue from the tail, building a page write descriptor from the work request with full range. Entries from another superblock are either returned to the dirty tail when bound to one superblock or terminate the scan for the caller to switch superblocks. Entries that are new or being freed are returned to the tail. Entries already under writeback are deferred to a later queue when integrity sync is not demanded, otherwise the scanner sleeps for completion and restarts because the entry may have vanished. Otherwise the entry is marked under writeback to pin it, written with a per superblock chunk budget, and progress accounting subtracts remaining budget and skipped pages with clamping at zero. Hung task progress is signaled at half timeout. Scheduling fairness flushes pending IO before yielding. After IO the entry is requeued by dirtiness and completion is signaled under combined locks with migration handling, and the scan exits early after modest time or budget exhaustion once progress occurred, counting fully clean entries additionally.

Cross superblock draining repeatedly takes the tail entry, attempts a nonblocking shared hold on its superblock, and on failure returns the entry to the tail to avoid spinning before continuing. On success it runs per superblock writeback under that hold, releases, and applies the same early exit on time and budget exhaustion once progress occurred, leaving unwritten entries queued. A small bounded helper wraps this with plug handling and initial queue fill when the IO queue starts empty.

The central writeback loop consumes a page budget until exhaustion, yields when background or kupdate work faces queued explicit work, and halts background work below its threshold. Each iteration records tracing, fills the IO queue when empty with age cutoff selection that distinguishes kupdate expiry from background immediacy, then dispatches to bound or unbound draining. Any progress or a first pass without prior queuing continues; otherwise an empty defer queue ends the loop, while a nonempty defer queue sleeps on the tail deferred entry to avoid spinning.

Work dispatch marks running state, then drains explicitly queued requests one by one with execution tracing and completion signaling, accumulating written counts. After the queue empties it sequentially probes full scan, dontcache, periodic, and background triggers in that order before clearing running state. Explicit dequeue removes the head under interrupt safe work protection and returns absent when empty.

Four opportunistic triggers share a cyclic non integrity style. Background runs with unbounded budget only above threshold. Periodic is disabled by zero interval, otherwise gated by expiry of last flush plus interval before using the global dirty count with kupdate marking. Full scan runs only when its flag is set, using a split share of global dirty pages and the stored reason before clearing the flag. Dontcache runs only when its flag was atomically taken, using its summed dontcache dirty count.

The flush worker names itself after its device. On the normal path, including shutdown even under rescuer, it repeatedly runs dispatch until no explicit work remains. Under rescuer with a registered device it instead performs one bounded write of 1024 pages. Afterwards it either wakes immediately when explicit work remains or arms a delayed wake when dirty IO exists and periodic writeback is enabled.

Dirty timestamp writeback wakes every writeback object that holds dirty timestamp entries by walking all devices under read side protection, then re arms itself after a rounded delay only when its expiry interval is nonzero. Its interval control handler applies generic integer range handling then either schedules immediate work when enabled or synchronously cancels when disabled. Initialization schedules the first delayed run when enabled and registers the control table, always reporting success.

Superblock flag parsing consults two lexical tables. The set table recognizes five names that set bits and record mask coverage, while the clear table recognizes four names that clear bits and likewise record coverage; unknown names report a distinct not a parameter signal.

Monolithic parsing tolerates absent input as success, first extracts security options, then repeatedly extracts keys with the supplied splitter, skips empties, splits at the first separator while ignoring a leading separator, and feeds each pair to string parsing until failure. The comma splitter uses comma separation. Counted string adaptation duplicates with termination, selects string versus flag type by presence, delegates, and releases.

Reconfigure contexts are refused for internal superblocks. Source assignment requires an exact key and string type, rejects duplicates, and transfers ownership with nulling of the donor. Parameter failures log through a helper that records a message and returns an invalid argument status.

Logging selects severity mapping for warning, error, info, and default notice when no context log exists, formatting with optional prefix. With a context log it appends a level tagged line into a fixed power of two ring indexed by head mask, discarding the oldest entry with release when full, tracking heap ownership per slot, and advancing head; allocation failure stores a static out of memory marker without ownership.

Queue mutation and state inspection serialize under the writeback list lock with inode lock nesting for state changes; the list lock is released before sleeping for writeback completion and reacquired on restart. Shared superblock holds protect per superblock draining. Explicit work queue uses interrupt safe work locking. Global device walks use read side critical sections. Duplicated contexts reinitialize their user API mutex. Dontcache marking uses atomic bit operations with a reference held across wakeup.

The writeback work descriptor aggregates a page budget with sync mode plus a cyclic range request and a reason code, alongside purpose markers for background and kupdate and integrity sync, with tagged and expiry controls and an optional bound superblock and a completion handle carrying progress stamp and wait queue plus list linkage. The page write descriptor derived from it adds dirty age cutoff with write chunk size and remaining and skipped counters plus an attached inode.

The filesystem context aggregates superblock flag values with mask plus source string ownership and an operation vector with parse and duplicate hooks, alongside type and network and user namespaces with credentials and security blob and error log with ring state, plus private and filesystem info pointers and a user API mutex. Parameters carry key with value kind and string and size. Constant entries pair names with numeric values. The log holds head and tail counters with a fixed buffer array and a heap ownership mask. The dirtytime control entry holds name with data pointer and length and mode and handler and minimum.

Inode writeback states distinguish new with freeing and will free and under sync and dirty variants. New or freeing entries never enter periodic writeout and are returned. Under sync entries encountered without integrity demand are deferred for a later pass; with integrity demand the waiter sleeps then restarts. Entry into writeout sets under sync as a memory pin that delays eviction until completion signaling after requeue.

Writeback object flags sequence running with start all carrying stored reason and start dontcache and registered. Running brackets dispatch. Start all persists across dispatch until cleared after one probe. Start dontcache is atomically taken exactly once per request. Periodic last flush timestamp advances on each due probe. Queue states cycle among dirty with IO and more IO and dirty time with tail selection and head refill.

Entry points comprise the workqueue flush handler with the dontcache kick and the global and per superblock wakeups, alongside the delayed dirtytime waker with the sysctl interval handler and the boot initializer that schedules dirtytime work and registers controls, plus the main filesystem parameter parser and the reconfigure constructor.

Hazards include inode disappearance across sleeps requiring restart, with superblock hold contention requiring tail return rather than spin and busy looping on deferred entries requiring sleep. Lost wakeups require re arm checks, with plug flushing before voluntary schedule and hung task false positives mitigated by half timeout wakeups. Ring overwrite needs correct release, with out of memory during string duplication or log formatting and duplicate source assignment and missing keys and non string sources and leading separators in monolithic input all requiring clean failure.

Mount vocabulary fixes set and clear mappings. The name dirsync selects value SB_DIRSYNC with masking, and separately the name lazytime selects value SB_LAZYTIME with masking, and separately the name mand selects value SB_MANDLOCK with masking, and separately the name ro selects value SB_RDONLY with masking, and separately the name sync selects value SB_SYNCHRONOUS with masking. Clearing uses the name async for value SB_SYNCHRONOUS, and separately nolazytime for SB_LAZYTIME, and separately nomand for SB_MANDLOCK, and separately rw for SB_RDONLY.

Control and error vocabulary fixes the dirtytime control name dirtytime_expire_seconds with mode 0644 and lower bound zero under vm, and separately sync mode WB_SYNC_NONE for opportunistic work with WB_SYNC_ALL for integrity wait, and separately reason WB_REASON_BACKGROUND with WB_REASON_PERIODIC and WB_REASON_DONTCACHE and WB_REASON_FORKER_THREAD, and separately purpose FS_CONTEXT_FOR_RECONFIGURE with FS_CONTEXT_FOR_SUBMOUNT, and separately parameter kinds fs_value_is_flag with fs_value_is_string, and separately failures ENOPARAM for unknown or deferred parameters with EINVAL for invalid values plus ENOMEM and EOPNOTSUPP for allocation and missing duplicator cases, and separately log prefix derived from module name.
